## Problem statement

`proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py` contains a dead assignment, `app = None`, that is immediately redefined by `with _status_endpoint(...) as app:`. Ruff reports it as **F811** ("Redefinition of unused `app`"), so lint runs are not clean and the test helper reads as if the value mattered when it cannot.

## Users

- **Proxy maintainer** — as a maintainer, I want the busy-engine regression harness free of dead assignments so lint output is clean and the helper's intent is unambiguous.
- **Implementing agent** — as an agent picking this up, I want a precise, low-risk scope so the fix is a one-line removal with no behavioural guessing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The dead `app = None` assignment in `call_local_status` (currently line 225) is removed, so `app` is bound only by the `with _status_endpoint(...) as app:` context manager.
- [ ] `ruff check proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py --select F811` reports zero findings (it currently reports 1 at line 228).
- [ ] The `REFACTOR-LP-0MW8QY8HE0051UNZ` marker comment block at the top of the file is removed once the smell is resolved.
- [ ] The file's existing tests still pass via `/skill:test` (changed scope), confirming the change is behaviour-neutral.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Hygiene-only, no behaviour change:** the assignment is dead because the `with … as app` rebinds the name before first use; test logic and assertions must not be altered.
- **Path correction:** the work-item description points at the now-removed worktree `.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MW3ED3XN003TPXI-…/proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py`; the authoritative file is the main-checkout path `proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py`.
- **Isolation:** implementation must occur in the worktree created by the implement skill, not the main checkout.
- No ruff configuration or CI lint gate was found in the repo; the finding originates from the refactor skill's linter run, not a build gate.

## Existing state

- `ruff check proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py --select F811` reproduces the finding:

  ```text
  F811 Redefinition of unused `app` from line 225
     --> proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py:228:10
  225 |     app = None
  226 |     with _status_endpoint(
  ...
  228 |     ) as app:
  help: Remove definition: `app`
  ```

- The file opens with a refactor-skill annotation block (lines 1–5) that records this work item and smell:

  ```python
  # <!-- REFACTOR-LP-0MW8QY8HE0051UNZ
  # smell: unused_import
  # severity: critical
  # description: Redefinition of unused `app` from line 219: `app` redefined here
  # -->
  ```

- `_status_endpoint` (line 147) is a `@contextlib.contextmanager` that yields `app` imported from `proxy.server`; the `with … as app` therefore always supplies a non-`None` value.

## Desired change

1. Delete the `app = None` line from `call_local_status`.
2. Delete the `REFACTOR-LP-0MW8QY8HE0051UNZ` marker block from the file header.
3. Re-run the ruff F811 check (expect zero findings) and the file's tests (expect unchanged pass).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_slots_busy_engine_policy.py` — Remove dead `app = None` at line 225 and the refactor marker block at lines 1–5.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `app = None` is genuinely dead — confirmed by reading the helper: the `with … as app` executes before the first use and always yields a value.
- **Risk (low):** removing the assignment could expose an import-cycle or name-shadowing issue if `_status_endpoint` failed before binding; the context manager always yields, so this is not expected, and the changed-scope test run will catch it.
- **Risk (low):** the description's line numbers (219/222) are stale relative to the current file (225/228) because the marker block shifted lines; the implementer must locate the code by content, not by fixed line number.
- **Scope-creep guard:** unrelated lint findings in the same file are out of scope; record any such findings as separate work items rather than expanding this one.

## Goal

A session whose own `Fallback triggered` line carries the same `turn=` id as its
first remote `Stream started` is attributed to that line's `reason` with
`fallback_attribution == own_fallback`, even when the fallback line is
timestamped **after** the remote stream (the pre-flight-buffering order). Parent:
LP-0MW0FFW8K002U0KQ (AC1, AC2).

## Context

`aggregation._attribute_fallback()` filters `e.session == session_id and e.ts <= first_remote_ts`
**before** `_same_turn()`, so the proxy's real order
`[remote] POST` → `Stream started` → `Stream finished` → `Fallback triggered`
(all the same turn) drops the matching line and the session falls through to
`unattributed`. This item is the tracer bullet: fixture + red test + the minimal
own-fallback tier change, all in one branch so the tree is green at the end.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` reproduces the
  observed order (`[remote] POST` → `Stream started` → `Stream finished` →
  `Fallback triggered`, all with the same `turn=`, fallback ~2 ms after the finish)
  and is used by a new test in `tests/test_turn_correlation.py`.
- That test asserts `fallback_reason` equals the fallback line's reason
  (e.g. `local_concurrency_limit`) and `fallback_attribution ==
  aggregation.FALLBACK_ATTRIBUTION_OWN_FALLBACK`.
- TDD evidence: the test is written first and observed failing with the
  `unattributed` state before the fix; the failure is recorded in the commit
  message or the item comment.
- Turn-first selection lives in one shared picker used by the own-fallback tier:
  an exact `turn=` match on the session's own line wins regardless of timestamp;
  evidence without a turn id keeps the `e.ts <= first_remote_ts` rule.
- `remote_move_time` never moves later than the first remote stream — a late
  matched line still yields a move time at/before `first_remote_ts`, so
  `context_at_fallback` anchoring is unchanged; asserted by a test.
- Changed-scope test gate passes for `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`.

- Parent AC1 (LP-0MW0FFW8K002U0KQ) is satisfied: A session whose own `Fallback triggered` line shares the first remote stream's `turn=` id is attributed to that line's `reason`, even when the fallback line is timestamped **after** the remote `Stream started` (the pre-flight-buffering ordering), instead of being labelled `unattributed`.
- Parent AC2 (LP-0MW0FFW8K002U0KQ) is satisfied: A regression test reproduces the observed ordering (`[remote] POST` → `Stream started` → `Stream finished` → `Fallback triggered`, all carrying the same `turn=`) and asserts the session's `fallback_reason` is the fallback line's reason and `fallback_attribution == own_fallback`.
**Key Files:**

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — `_attribute_fallback()`, `_build_session()`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_turn_correlation.py`

## Notes

- `proxy/` is read-only for this item (`_preflight_streaming_response()` /
  `_handle_streaming_success()` explain the ordering).

## Goal

When the progress source is unavailable, behaviour falls back to today's liveness-only extension (fail-safe, logged once), and the unobservable case is counted/attributable via a metric.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fail-safe fallback.** If progress cannot be observed (per-slot query fails, aggregate query fails, or llama.cpp build lacks progress fields), the lease extension falls back to liveness-only + the adaptive acquisition estimate — the same behaviour as today, but explicitly documented and tested.
- **AC2 — Unobservable metric.** A new counter metric `proxy_prefill_progress_unobservable_total` increments each time progress is unobservable during a lease poll. This is visible in monitoring (Prometheus / statsd), not only a log line.
- **AC3 — Throttled warning.** The existing throttled warning (`_PREFILL_WARN_INTERVAL`, default 60 s) continues to fire but now co-occurs with the metric increment so both logging and observability capture the event.
- **AC4 — No behavioural regression.** When the progress source works, the fail-safe path is never taken — no spurious warnings, no spurious metric increments.

- **AC6 — Failure semantics.** If the progress source is unavailable, behaviour falls back to today's liveness-only extension (fail-safe, logged once), never to an unbounded extension.
- **AC11 — Unobservable case stays fail-safe and countable.** It keeps today's estimate + liveness behaviour, still logs the WARNING, and is now counted/attributable (a metric, not only a log line) so a persistent rate is visible.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`

## Dependencies

- LP-0MW8VMJYL009K9UB (Test fixtures for measured prefill scenarios) — provides fixtures.

## Deliverables

- New metric definition in `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (counter: `prefill_progress_unobservable_total`).
- Metric increment call in `_query_prefill_progress` and/or `_extend_lease_during_prefill` when progress is unobservable.
- Tests asserting the fail-safe path fires correctly when progress source is broken.

## Goal

**As** the implementer of cold-regime calibration, **I want** the cold-only fit rows written and failing first, **so that** warm-sample exclusion, the p75 uplift on the cold distribution and the documented rollbacks are pinned before any production code changes.

Parent AC1 and AC5 (test half). **Test-first**: the `[impl] Cold-only prefill rate window` item depends on this one.

## Scope

Add calibration rows to `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_cold_fit.py` (a new module; the existing `test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` gains only the small-prompt no-regression row). Seed windows with synthetic observed samples via `proxy.prefill_eta.reset()` and the `_seed_varied` pattern already used in `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py`, so every row is deterministic and names its rate basis in the assertion message.

**Out:** production code, config changes, docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Warm/cache-hit samples never price the cold rate.** A window mixing instant cache hits (`measured_cached_ratio >= 0.90`, service < 1000 ms, `processed_tokens` near 0) with cold large samples (`measured_cached_ratio < 0.10`, `processed_tokens >= 32000`) yields a cold `prefill_ms_per_token` fitted **only** from the cold samples; the row also asserts the mixed-window rate is materially more optimistic (so a regression to a mixed fit fails loudly).
- **AC2 — Cold-sample predicate.** Samples are admitted to the cold fit only when `measured_cached_ratio < 0.10` **and** `processed_tokens >= 32000`; rows at the boundaries (ratio 0.0999/0.10, tokens 31 999/32 000) assert inclusion/exclusion.
- **AC3 — Rollback rows.** `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile: 0` returns the cold point estimate byte-for-byte (coefficients compared with `==`, not approximately), and `local_admission_guard_policy: observe` / `off` never refuse.
- **AC4 — Small-prompt calibration unchanged.** A below-32 000-token prompt prices exactly as it does today (same coefficients as the pre-change mixed window), so the cold work cannot degrade the existing small-prompt fit.
- **AC5 — No-regression guard rows.** The existing conservative-pricing rows in `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` still describe the shipped behaviour; any row this change invalidates is updated here with a comment naming the new basis.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_cold_fit.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py`
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`

# Proxy owns the audit admission budget and exposes availability

## Goal

Make the `llm` proxy the **single authority for the audit admission budget** — the audit cap and the live audit-lease registry — and expose it so every dispatcher host queries one source instead of each ContextHub host asserting its own `budget.json` cap.

**Parent:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (Serialise audits at the shared local resource). **Producer direction (2026-11-09):** `budget.json` is managed per ContextHub host and ContextHub may run on several servers; the proxy is the one shared component, so it owns the budget and ContextHub queries it.

## Problem

The audit cap today lives in `~/.herdr/downtime/budget.json` (`maxAudit`) on each ContextHub host, and the live ledger is `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json`. With ContextHub on two or more servers, each host can independently believe it is under cap while together they oversubscribe the one local `llama-server` GPU. The proxy already sees every client host (`client_ip`, `X-Session-Id`) and already issues local-admission tickets (`admission_reserve.py`, `POST /llama/local/reserve`), so it is the natural owner of a single audit budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Proxy-owned cap.** The proxy config owns an audit admission cap (`audit_admission.max_audits`, default `1`) and the live audit-lease registry. For audit admission the proxy no longer relies on a client-supplied cap; a client may still send a requested cap, which is clamped to the proxy's configured maximum.
- **AC2 — Availability read.** A read endpoint (e.g. `GET /llama/local/audit/availability`) returns `{cap, live, available, leases: [{session_id, client_ip, acquired_at, expires_at}]}` with the same vocabulary the dispatcher logs. A second audit acquire beyond the cap is refused with a stable reason token (`audit-budget-saturated`) and a wait/retry hint.
- **AC3 — Single mutation path.** Acquire/renew/release endpoints are the only way to change the live audit-lease set (reusing the audit-tier lease from AC1 of the parent, or a sibling module). A refused acquire performs no partial state change.
- **AC4 — Staleness and crash recovery.** A lease older than its TTL is reclaimed and the reclamation is logged (`audit_lease_reclaimed reason=expired`); a crashed holder cannot wedge the budget. Clock comparisons use the proxy's clock only.
- **AC5 — Backwards compatible.** An existing per-host `budget.json` is no longer authoritative for audit admission; at startup the proxy logs a warning if it detects a conflicting client-side cap, and the migration is documented.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** Unit/integration tests cover: cap enforcement (cap=1 admits one, refuses the second), the `audit-budget-saturated` refusal and hint, clean release, TTL reclamation, availability read agreeing with lease state, and fail-safe behaviour on an unreadable registry. Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC7 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`proxy/docs/routing.md`, the audit-budget section, and the ContextHub cross-reference).
- **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

- **AC1 — Proxy-side audit admission token (parent AC1).** A proxy-side audit admission token exists such that at most one audit-tier session holds it across all client hosts; a second audit waits rather than competing. The token is identified and released for the whole audit lifetime, with a TTL/staleness backstop.
## Out of scope

- The ContextHub-side query change (separate item in the ContextHub worklog).
- The audit-skill client that acquires the lease (parent AC2 / SorraAgents).
- Implement-tier budget ownership (only the audit tier moves to the proxy).
- Slot count, context size, prefill cap.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — audit-tier lease registry and cap, or a sibling `audit_budget.py`.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — availability/acquire/renew/release endpoints.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — audit-tier denial and queueing in the local dispatch path.
- `proxy/config.yaml` / config loader — `audit_admission.max_audits` (default 1).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — audit budget ownership, release points, failure modes.
- `proxy/tests/` — new audit-budget suite.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the proxy is reachable from every ContextHub host (it already proxies their model traffic).
- **Risk:** moving the cap to the proxy means a proxy restart resets in-memory leases; mitigation is a persisted registry or an explicit fail-safe on restart, decided in implementation.
- **Scope-creep guard:** extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
data.title: Proxy owns the audit admission budget and exposes availability

Unit tests covering the SorraAgents audit-batch queue with project-aware entries and cross-project `items_included` reporting.

**Parent:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (Serialise audits at the shared local resource). **Covers:** Parent AC6 (testing/validation), Parent AC4 (tested and documented).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Project-aware queue entries.** A test asserts that queue entries carry a project/worklog root identity.
- **AC2 — Cross-project serialisation.** A test asserts that an audit dispatched for repo A and one for repo B are serialised by the same queue (one waits for the other).
- **AC3 — items_included reporting.** A test asserts that the batch drain reports `items_included` across projects.
- **AC4 — Each item drains against its own worklog root.** A test asserts that each drained item routes to the correct worklog.
- **AC5 — Changed-scope tests pass.** Running changed-scope tests via the test skill passes after the SorraAgents implementation lands.

## Deliverables

- SorraAgents audit skill test module for the batch queue.
- Test coverage documented in the audit skill documentation.

# SorraAgents: Cross-project audit-batch queue

## Goal

Make the audit skill's batch queue project-aware so audits from different repositories are serialised and each drains against its own worklog root.

**Parent:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (Serialise audits at the shared local resource). **Covers:** Parent AC2 (cross-project audit-batch queue).

## Problem

The audit skill's batch queue lives at `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores/audit-batch` and is host-wide, but entries carry no project identity. A drain from repo A can dequeue an item meant for repo B, and there is no `items_included` reporting across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Project identity in queue entries.** `QueueEntry` (or the equivalent in `SorraAgents/skill/shared/queue.py`) carries a project/worklog root field.
- **AC2 — Cross-project serialisation.** Audits dispatched for different repos are serialised through the same queue — a second audit waits when one is draining.
- **AC3 — Correct worklog routing.** Each drained item routes to its own worklog root, not a shared default.
- **AC4 — items_included reporting.** The batch drain reports `items_included` showing contributions from each project.
- **AC5 — Existing single-host behaviour preserved.** One audit per host still holds; the new gate narrows to one audit across hosts.

## Deliverables

- `SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — acquire/renew/release the audit lease around a run; make batch-queue entries project-aware.
- `SorraAgents/skill/shared/queue.py` — carry a project/worklog root in `QueueEntry`.
- Documentation updates in the audit skill.

## Dependencies

- **LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK** — Proxy owns the audit admission budget (the lease mechanism).

# Integration test: Concurrent audit dispatch from two hosts

## Goal

Integration test that simulates two concurrent audit dispatches from two different hosts (distinct client identities) and verifies that one runs and one waits, with a log line per decision.

**Parent:** LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (Serialise audits at the shared local resource). **Covers:** Parent AC4 (tested and documented — two concurrent dispatches), Parent AC6 (testing/validation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — One running, one waiting.** Two concurrent audit dispatches from two different hosts (simulated distinct client identities) result in one running and one waiting.
- **AC2 — Log line per decision.** A log line is emitted per decision (admitted vs. waiting).
- **AC3 — Cross-host serialisation.** The serialisation is enforced at the proxy level, not per-host.
- **AC4 — Changed-scope tests pass.** Running changed-scope tests via the test skill passes after all implementation lands.

## Deliverables

- Integration test module covering concurrent audit dispatch from multiple hosts.

data.description:
## Problem

The group-1 programme cannot progress by dispatch: its work-item graph contains a **dependency cycle**.

```
LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4  (Group 1 validation: restart + measure)
        │  depends-on
        ├──────────────► LP-0MW7V292T0020G02  (impl: 38k cold threshold when residency unmeasured)
        │                        │  contains child
        │                        └────────────► LP-0MW81DWXN003XFMR  (Verify group restart and dated-title handoff, AC7/AC8)
        │                                                 │  depends-on
        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` has outbound `depends-on` edges to `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` and `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI`, so `implement.py parent` reports `blocked-parent` for every child and refuses to start (`parent_blocked_reason=outbound-dependency+status-blocked`).
- `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` cannot reach a terminal stage because child 8 `LP-0MW81DWXN003XFMR` is `blocked` — and it is blocked on `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4`.

Neither item can ever start. The `wl` dependency checker did not flag this because the edge is transitive through a child relationship, not a direct pair.

## Evidence

- `wl dep list LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4 --json` → outbound: `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` (open), `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI` (open).
- `wl dep list LP-0MW81DWXN003XFMR --json` → outbound: `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (blocked) plus three `completed` siblings.
- `implement.py parent LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4 --json` → `blocked: true`, all five children `blocked-parent`, nothing started.
- `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` children 1–7 are all `completed`/`in_review` and their commits are in `dev` (e.g. `011f2db0c LP-0MW81DUBK005QRFQ`); only child 8 is outstanding.

## Root cause

Child 8's scope is **inherently downstream of the validation item it gates**: it exists to verify the group restart and the dated-title handoff (impl AC7/AC8), which are precisely `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4`'s AC1/AC2/AC6. Wiring it as a blocking child of `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` makes the implementation epic wait for its own verification.

## Resolution options

1. **Preferred — retire the redundant child.** Close `LP-0MW81DWXN003XFMR` as a duplicate of `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (its verification content is fully covered by that item's AC1/AC2/AC6, which already record the restart PIDs, deployed HEAD, `/health` JSON, group-2 absence and the dated-title dispositions). `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` then has all children terminal and can advance to `in_review`.
2. **Alternative — re-wire the edge.** Remove `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4 → LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` and depend instead on the impl's substantive children (all `in_review`), leaving child 8 gated on the validation item as designed.

Option 1 was not executed by the implement session that raised this item: closing another item and rewiring plan-authored edges is a producer decision. This item records the defect so it is not lost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — The cycle is broken.** At least one of the two options above is applied, and `wl dep list` on both items shows no cycle.
- **AC2 — No coverage lost.** Whichever option is chosen, the restart + dated-title verification still has a single, named owner with a recorded outcome.
- **AC3 — Verified unblocked.** `implement.py parent LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4 --json` no longer reports `blocked-parent` for the cycle reason, and `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` reaches `completed`/`in_review` (or is documented as intentionally still open).
- **AC4 — Regression guard considered.** State whether `wl dep add` / plan-time dependency review should detect transitive child cycles; if yes, file the follow-up.
data.title: Group-1 dispatch deadlock: validation item waits on an impl epic whose verification child waits on the validation item
